name: Bandex
description: A compound that temporarily up-regulates the SNT interface layer between organic neural tissue and BCI hardware, dramatically increasing the bandwidth of data transfer between brain and machine. Developed by Helix as part of their SNT research program, Bandex was quietly shelved after clinical trials showed a narrow therapeutic window between 'significantly enhanced BCI performance' and 'irreversible SNT degradation.' The formula leaked and hit the street within a year. At correct dosing, Bandex allows a user to process and act on BCI data — network feeds, augment inputs, sensor arrays — at speeds that blur the line between human and machine cognition.
effects: Simultaneous multi-channel BCI operation without cognitive lag
Latency between neural intent and augment response reduced to near-zero
Enhanced integration of external data feeds (network, sensor, comms) into conscious awareness
Hackers report the ability to perceive network architecture as spatial environment
side_effects: SNT degradation at the interface layer — cumulative and irreversible
Cognitive bleed: BCI data intrudes into non-BCI thought (involuntary data hallucinations)
Migraines from vascular pressure at SNT sites
Risk of BCI system crash if bandwidth exceeds hardware limits
Long-term: progressive loss of boundary between organic thought and machine input
cultural_context: Helix's decision to shelve Bandex was formally attributed to safety concerns, but internal documents (leaked on the net) suggest the real reason was that Bandex worked too well — it demonstrated that SNT interfaces could be pushed far beyond their rated capacity, which threatened the company's roadmap for selling incremental BCI hardware upgrades. The drug is beloved by netrunners and information brokers for whom BCI bandwidth is directly correlated with income and survival. The SNT degradation is known and accepted — most heavy users reason that they'll have enough money to buy a full SNT replacement before the damage catches up with them.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 netrunner who has been using Bandex for two years is now experiencing involuntary data hallucinations 24 hours a day — network ghosts bleeding into her vision — and she can't tell anymore which of her thoughts are hers and which are machine noise.

Helix has quietly hired a fixer to recover all existing street stock of Bandex ahead of a new product launch — suggesting their upcoming BCI hardware release has a critical vulnerability that Bandex use would expose.

A the Gray Zone hacker discovered that at maximum Bandex effect, he briefly accessed a data layer he wasn't supposed to be able to reach — something encrypted and vast, running underneath GLMZ's civilian network — and now people with military-grade chrome are asking him very politely to forget what he saw.
